# The T1w/T2w Ratio for Myelin Mapping {.unnumbered}

{{< include "../includes/WIP-callout.qmd" >}}

A recurring goal of quantitative MRI is a map of myelin content. One popular and
inexpensive approach uses only two ordinary structural scans — a T1-weighted and
a T2-weighted image — and forms their ratio. This resource describes the idea and,
importantly, the reasons to be cautious about interpreting it as a myelin measure.

## The idea

The T1w/T2w method was introduced by Glasser and Van Essen (2011) as a way to map
cortical areas from myelin content (@fig-t1t2-glasser-vanessen). Both a
T1-weighted and a T2-weighted image carry a similar receive-coil intensity bias,
but that bias divides out in their *ratio*, while the myelin-related contrast in
the two images reinforces. The resulting T1w/T2w map enhances myelin contrast and
is generalizable across 3 T scanners and pulse sequences without any special
acquisition. Mapped to the cortical surface, the spatial gradients of the group
map agree well with cytoarchitectonic areal borders, so the ratio became a widely
used, low-cost proxy for cortical myelination.

![Glasser and Van Essen (2011) introduced the T1w/T2w ratio to map cortical areas
by myelin content; the ratio cancels the shared receive-coil intensity bias.](images/t1t2-ratio-glasser-vanessen.png){#fig-t1t2-glasser-vanessen}

## Why the ratio is not a specific myelin measure

The convenience of the method should not be mistaken for validity. A series of
studies comparing the T1w/T2w ratio against histology and against more direct
myelin-MRI measures — quantitative susceptibility mapping, magnetization transfer
saturation, and multi-echo myelin water fraction (MWF) — find that the ratio does
not track myelin specifically, especially in white matter
(@fig-t1t2-critique-1, @fig-t1t2-critique-2).

Several findings recur across this literature. In the corpus callosum the T1w/T2w
map does not positively correlate with Luxol-fast-blue optical density and shows,
if anything, a weak negative correlation, whereas myelin water fraction correlates
strongly and positively with the histology. Direct method comparisons find only
weak correlations between the T1w/T2w ratio and both SyMRI relaxometry and MT
saturation, even though those two agree well with each other. And reliability is
not the issue — the ratio is highly reproducible test–retest — but reproducibility
is not validity: a measure can be stable yet still fail to reflect the quantity of
interest. The reasonable summary is that the T1w/T2w ratio may correlate with
myelin at the cortical level but is not a specific map of myelin density in white
matter, and should be used with that limitation in mind.

![Studies reporting a discrepancy between T1w/T2w maps and histology, and weak
correlations with other myelin-MRI measures.](images/t1t2-ratio-critique-1.png){#fig-t1t2-critique-1}

![Test–retest and concurrent-validity comparisons: the T1w/T2w ratio is reliable
but has low criterion validity as an index of myelin, particularly in white and
subcortical structures.](images/t1t2-ratio-critique-2.png){#fig-t1t2-critique-2}
